headline: Malaysia backs the Rohingya genocide case. Its Immigration Act has no word for refugee.
context: The World Court is due to rule on 19 Nov in The Gambia's genocide case against Myanmar. Malaysia backs the case but did not intervene. UNHCR lists 129,400 Rohingya refugees and asylum-seekers in Malaysia.

cards.big: Malaysia backs The Gambia's genocide case against Myanmar, its foreign minister told an OIC meeting on 24 Sep. The World Court is due to rule on 19 Nov.
cards.sub: At the UN in 2025, Malaysia said Myanmar's 1982 Citizenship Law 'has systematically denied the Rohingya people their fundamental rights.'
trace: Support for the case: Stage 3 VERIFIED against Malaysia's Foreign Ministry statement at the OIC Annual Coordination Meeting, UN headquarters, 24 Sep 2026, para 9 ('the government expressly supports the case'); Bernama 25 Sep 2026 [6a] reports the same. Stage 3 INCORRECT on the date: 25 Sep was Bernama's publication date; event date 24 Sep (Bernama's own report says the speech was on Thursday).
Diplomatic support, not intervention: ICJ case 178 page [1] lists 11 intervening States; Malaysia is not among them. Stated in the context field (Stage 2 OVERCLAIM fix).
Judgment date: ICJ press release 2026/27, 3 Nov 2026 [2a]; Stage 3 VERIFIED; wording changed to 'is due to rule' per Stage 3.
Quote: Stage 3 VERIFIED against the Foreign Ministry's published text of Permanent Representative Ahmad Faisal Muhamad's statement, 30 Sep 2025; UN transcript [5] matches but is machine-generated.

cards.big: The Immigration Act has no refugee category. Rohingya with UNHCR cards remain PATI, the official term for illegal immigrants, the National Security Council said on 10 Sep.
cards.sub: They are exempt from prosecution only for lacking papers and overstaying. Working without a valid pass or permit is an offence.
trace: No refugee category: Stage 3 VERIFIED against Act 155 (2006 reprint) [9a] and the 2026 Immigration (Amendment) Act, which adds no refugee or asylum category and leaves ss.6, 15 and 55 unchanged.

'remain PATI': National Security Council (MKN) portal, 10 Sep 2026, 'Pemegang kad UNHCR masih tertakluk kepada undang-undang imigresen' [26a], which says Rohingya holding UNHCR cards are still categorised as PATI and credits the Immigration Department. Stage 3 used the same MKN notice. Immigration's 31 Jul statement (Bernama BM, 'Pemegang Kad UNHCR Masih Dianggap PATI') [26b] says the same. Paraphrase, no quotation marks: the MKN wording was read in summary.

Two exemptions only: MKN 10 Sep [26a] (Stage 3 VERIFIED: exemptions for lacking valid documents or pass and for overstaying); RTM [26c] 'Pengecualian hanya melibatkan dua kesalahan'. Working without a valid pass or permit: MKN [26a], Stage 3 VERIFIED substance, 'valid pass or permit' wording kept.

cards.big: Malaysia's own refugee registration began on 1 Jan with 4,010 detainees in Peninsular depots. By June, 78 Rohingya had been approved as refugees, the Home Minister said.
cards.sub: The DPP card it issues is a time-limited Special Pass under 1963 immigration rules. Only those in Malaysia before 2023 qualify.
trace: 1 Jan 2026 start: Stage 3 VERIFIED (Home Ministry statement 30 Oct 2026, para 9; UNHCR notice 2 Jan 2026). Reported in Kosmo/Utusan 30 Oct [27a][27b].

4,010 detainees in Peninsular depots: Stage 3 VERIFIED (Home Ministry DPP page; Dewan Rakyat 13 Oct 2026), recommended 'initial Peninsular Malaysia cohort'. RTM and Berita Harian report Phase 1 as 4,010 detainees in immigration depots across Peninsular Malaysia [28b].

78 Rohingya approved by June: Home Minister Saifuddin Nasution's written reply, reported 9 Jul 2026 by Malay Mail [14a], Utusan [14b] and Sinar Harian [28a] ('78 tahanan etnik Rohingya … diluluskan status pelarian … setakat Jun'). Stage 3: the 78 total has official corroboration (Home Ministry DPP page); the 'by June' timing and Rohingya composition rest on the minister's reported reply, so the card attributes it to him. Not presented as a rate.

Special Pass: Stage 3 omitted fact, VERIFIED against the Home Ministry statement of 30 Oct 2026, para 10; Kosmo 30 Oct [27a]: 'Kad DPP merupakan suatu bentuk Pas Khas di bawah Peraturan 14, Peraturan-Peraturan Imigresen 1963 yang bersifat bertempoh'.
Before 2023: Home Ministry 30 Oct (Stage 3); RTM [27e] 'Pelarian tiba selepas Januari 2023 tidak dipertimbang untuk DPP'.
Dropped: 129,400 beside 78 (Stage 2 and Stage 3 MISLEADING_FRAMING; moved to context); 25 eligible for work (Stage 3 UNVERIFIED); 4,008 breakdown (UNVERIFIED); 2029 target (2029 vs 2030 unresolved).

cards.big: A return programme for 5,000 Myanmar nationals began on 29 Sep. Records traced so far show no Rohingya sent; their return was under discussion, the PM told Parliament.
cards.sub: Malaysia calls it voluntary. UNHCR, with no access to the 1,476 returned, questioned whether their choices were free and informed.
trace: 5,000-person programme, first phase 1,476 on 29 Sep: Stage 3 VERIFIED (Malaysia MADANI, PMO, 30 Sep 2026; UNHCR 30 Sep 2026). Home Ministry: first phase 'involving 1,476 Myanmar nationals'; programme not limited to Rohingya (The Rakyat Post 6 Oct [30a]).

PM, 6 Oct: Stage 3 VERIFIED against the PMO verbatim transcript and asked to restore the 'records checked so far' qualifier. Reported English rendering: 'Based on the records we have traced so far, no Rohingya individuals have been repatriated, but this is still under discussion' [30a]. Paraphrased without quotation marks (translation).

Voluntary: Home Ministry description of the programme (Stage 3, Al Jazeera, ABC). UNHCR press release 30 Sep 2026 [29a]: concerned by returns of 1,476 people; no access to the individuals; questions whether decisions were free and informed; calls for individual assessment and non-refoulement. Stage 3 omitted fact, VERIFIED.
Dropped: 'agreed to take back 5,000' Rohingya (Stage 2 MISLEADING_FRAMING; Stage 3 UNVERIFIED); ICJ 2020 order beside the returns (Stage 2: implied deportation into genocide).

cards.big: Abroad, Malaysia backs the genocide case for the Rohingya. At home, a Rohingya it recognises as a refugee holds a Special Pass.
trace: Restructures the question from 'does Malaysia recognise Rohingya refugees' to 'what does recognition mean in law'. Both halves verified: support for the case (hook trace); DPP card as a Special Pass under reg. 14 (fact 2 trace).

Replaces Stage 1's 'lacuna where the word refugee would go' (Stage 3 MISLEADING / UNDERCLAIM: omitted the Special Pass mechanism). 'Abroad' replaces 'In The Hague' so no reader infers Malaysia is a party or intervener (Stage 2).

cards.big: Whatever the World Court rules on 19 Nov, Malaysia's Immigration Act has no word for refugee. Malaysia chose a time-limited pass over a category in law.
cards.sub: Section 55 lets a minister exempt a class of persons by gazetted order. SUHAKAM warned in June of 'escalating hate and dehumanisation' of Rohingya.
trace: Present tense replaces 'wake up on 20 Nov' (Stage 3 OVERCLAIM: prediction). Re-check the Act at Phase 8 and after 19 Nov.

'chosen a time-limited pass over a category in law': editorial view, grounded in the Home Ministry's own design (DPP card as a reg. 14 Special Pass, 30 Oct 2026), the PM's 7 Oct 2026 position that Malaysia should decide refugee status itself [15d], and non-accession to the 1951 Convention [8a][8b]. STRENGTHENED (Stage 5): names the choice without attributing it to any community.
Section 55: Stage 3 VERIFIED (ss.55(1), 55(2); s.65(3) requires state concurrence for East Malaysia; unchanged by the 2026 amendment).
SUHAKAM: media statement 31/2026, 3 Jun 2026, 'SUHAKAM condemns escalating hate and dehumanisation of the Rohingya community' [23a]. INTRODUCED (Stage 6 self-verified).

synthesis_notes: Over-integration decisions. (1) Register: Stage 2 asked to drop the deadpan juxtaposition. Kept, because it is the editor's direction and the juxtapositions now carry the government's own descriptions (a 'voluntary' programme, a Special Pass, the 2023 cut-off) beside the criticism; the fix Stage 2 wanted, the government's stated rationale, is applied on cards 3 and 4 and in the reframe rather than by changing register. (2) Stage 5 asked the view to name 'Malay-Muslim' public hostility and electoral incentives as the driver. Rejected the ethnic attribution: Stage 5's own log labels the electoral claim MY_OPINION, the 3R bar requires two independent primary sources for claims about a community, and the house rule allows anger at process, not at groups. Adopted the verifiable core instead: the view names the policy choice (a time-limited pass over a category in law) and cites SUHAKAM's documented warning about hate, with no community named. (3) Stage 2 asked for Rohingya voices. The most-cited Malaysia-based Rohingya group (MERHROM) is the subject of a live Societies Act prosecution (The Star, 30 Sep 2026); quoting it risks prejudicing that case, and the other quoted voices are diaspora bodies. UNHCR's protection concern stands in on card 4; the gap is logged for a later edition. (4) Stage 2 asked for gender data and to name Teresa Kok: the depot breakdown is UNVERIFIED (Stage 3), so it stays off the cards; the parliamentary question is credited in the trace. (5) Stage 2 asked for the Economic lens: work access appears on card 2's source trail and on card 1 (working without a valid pass or permit); a full economic card would displace the Regional card, which carries the returns story. (6) Kept off the cards as before: UNHCR depot access (contested and dated), the 2022 Sungai Bakap escape (dated), and the PM hosting Myanmar's president on 8 Oct (Stage 3 verified it; held because one card cannot carry it without implying endorsement). Compression decisions: the PM's qualifier 'records traced so far' is kept; 'Peninsular' kept; '129,400' kept with its population definition in the context ('refugees and asylum-seekers'); 'valid pass or permit' kept. Elevated word: none; 'lacuna' was cut with the misleading reframe and no other word passed the no-substitute test. Post-verdict: after 17:00 MYT on 19 Nov, replace the hook's second sentence and the view's opening clause with the ruling's actual outcome and Malaysia's reaction, quoted verbatim from the judgment and an official statement, then run a Stage 3 delta check on those two cards only.
